name: Validated MPM Vehicle Water Coupling
goal: Develop a physically defensible simulation and validation basis for a flooded-road vehicle pipeline using 3D Gaussian splatting and MPM or closely related particle-based fluid-rigid coupling. THE KEY PHYSICAL GAP IS THAT THREE AR&R MASS CLASSES, SEDAN, LARGE PASSENGER VEHICLE AND 4WD, CURRENTLY USE THE SAME YARIS HULL WHILE ONLY THE MASS IS RELABELLED. Identify which geometry-dependent quantities must differ by class, which parameters can be scaled or calibrated and which require distinct geometry, and what validation evidence is needed before interpreting the sweep as class-specific.
summary:
A defensible FORD / NO-FORD result REQUIRES CLASS-SPECIFIC GEOMETRY and experimentally anchored force-stability validation, NOT a common Yaris hull with relabelled mass: buoyancy, drag and lift lever arms, wheel normal loads and sliding/float/roll thresholds depend jointly on displaced volume, underbody shape, wheelbase, track and centre of mass [Smi19, Mar17, Arr15, Alq22].

DIRECTLY APPLICABLE: full-scale stability tests measure traction, buoyancy and drag across three vehicle types and bed materials [Smi19]; moving-vehicle CFD reproduces a medium passenger-car experiment and reports 0.38 m floating and 0.39 m2/s depth-velocity thresholds ONLY FOR THAT TESTED CONFIGURATION [Alq22].
TRANSFERABLE COUPLING: SPH-multibody fording explicitly resolves suspension, wheels, tire/ground contact and particle-body coupling [Was15]; open SPH/non-smooth MBD coupling provides convergence tests and a reproducible reference architecture [Can18]. MPM offers two-way rigid coupling [Hu18], but free-surface incompressibility, particle disorder and contact require dedicated treatment [Zha17c, Zha17d, Li22b].
CLASS-SPECIFIC STATE REQUIRED: distinct geometry for hull dimensions and the submerged-volume curve, wheel locations, track and wheelbase, wetted and projected areas, contact patches, CoM and inertia, hence buoyancy, drag and lift moments, axle loads, traction and rollover margins. MASS ALONE MAY BE SCALED ONLY AFTER geometry-specific hydrostatics and inertia are established; regressions supply provisional CoM/inertia estimates, NOT VALIDATION [All03]. Watertightness is itself a model-form assumption that materially shifts flotation thresholds [Kra16, Boc19].
CLAIM-GRADE VALIDATION: verify force/momentum, hydrostatic equilibrium, free-surface dam-break/slosh and rigid-contact convergence BEFORE vehicle cases [Sun19c, Li14, Roa94]. Report experimental, parameter and discretisation uncertainty SEPARATELY [Obe04, Roy11, Cel07].
